patient_has_finding_of_moderate_major_de.assessment: The patient presents with low mood symptoms (anhedonia, guilt, hypersomnia, fatigue, trouble concentrating, increased appetite) consistent with major depressive disorder; no features suggest severe episode (psychosis, suicidality, gross impairment), so moderate severity is a plausible assignment.
patient_has_finding_of_moderate_major_de.evidence: She reports increased sleep and appetite over the past few months as well as difficulty concentrating on her schoolwork. She no longer enjoys spending time with her friends and feels guilty for not spending more time with her family.

patient_has_finding_of_moderately_severe.assessment: The chart does not describe impairment or symptom burden in the 'moderately severe' range (such as marked functional incapacity or agitation/retardation) nor does it grade severity explicitly; thus, no chart confirmation.

patient_has_finding_of_severe_major_depr.assessment: No evidence for severe major depression (no psychotic features, no suicidal ideation, no inability to function or perform self-care); moderate features more likely.
patient_has_finding_of_severe_major_depr.evidence: She is able to attend college, presents with symptoms consistent with moderate but not severe depression.
